key_insight: ABAQUS simulations show that optimized friction stir welding parameters can create a stable thermal window for joining dissimilar AA7075–AA2024 plates without reaching melting.
engineering_relevance: The study helps define process settings that support defect-free, structurally sound FSW joints for high-strength aluminum aerospace-grade materials.
method: Modeled dissimilar AA7075 and AA2024 plates in ABAQUS.
Simulated friction stir welding on 200 mm × 60 mm × 6 mm specimens.
Varied tool rotational speed, feed rate, and tilt angle to assess thermal and structural response.
evidence_signal: The simulations indicated a moderate peak temperature of about 580°C, which lies in the plasticization range of both alloys and below their melting points.
watch_item: The results are simulation-based, so experimental validation is still needed to confirm weld quality and mechanical performance in practice.
paper_title: Influence of Tib2 Reinforcement and Tool Traverse Speed on the Structural and Thermal Behavior of Dissimilar Metals (AA7075–AA2024) of Friction Stir Welded Joints: an ABAQUS Study
